metadata.note: Buffalo Creek & Gauley Railroad, Dundon - Widen, Clay County, West Virginia (18 mi). An Elk River Coal & Lumber Co. (J. G. Bradley) short line, incorporated April 1904, which carried passengers between the company towns of Widen and Swandale and the B&O at Dundon. It ran steam trains first and, from 1941, the Mack rail bus Motor A. Drawn 1920-1957 as a single feature: the BC&G operated under its own name throughout, so there is no Rule 4 split (the 1958 sale to Clinchfield/Pittston falls after the drawable end). Research report: research/branches/buffalo_creek_and_gauley_railroad.txt.

metadata.freight_only_audit: Applied at creation, 2026-10-26: not drawn are freight 1958-Feb 1965, the Majestic Mining coal reopening 1971-1985, the Elk River Railroad 1990s-1999 (to Avoca), the Elk River Coal & Lumber logging railroad Avoca - Lilly Fork (~9 mi, Shay-hauled company logging track, no public passenger evidence), and the Widen mine and Swandale mill spurs.
metadata.not_drawn: The Buffalo Creek & Gauley Co-op speeder excursions (from 2005, no dates of operation established) and the Rail Explorers pedal railbikes out of Dundon (from 8 June 2024). These are not trains, and the report advises against drawing them.
not_yet_sourced: bcg-dundon-widen START 1920 is [OPEN]: earliest confirmed year (Official Guide 16 June 1920). Service on the 1904-1911 partial line and 1911-1919 is unproven. Look in a 1905-1919 Official Guide, Poor's Manual, the ICC valuation docket, Clay County newspapers, or Fowler's West Virginia PDF (branchline.uk/jfpdf/westvirginiarrs.pdf, which could not be downloaded).

bcg-dundon-widen END 1957: last contemporary confirmation (Beebe & Clegg 1957). The true end is between 1957 and Nov 1959 (Guide: 'Freight service only'). american-rails' 'early 1959' is uncorroborated. A 1958 Guide card or a last-run newspaper story would settle it.
Headway (360 min) and avg_speed_kmh (20) are estimates from the 1920/1939/1951 Guide snapshots.

Source conflicts recorded, not resolved: incorporation 1 Apr 1904 (Wikipedia, american-rails) vs 7 Apr 1904 (Lewis 1975); abandonment 23 Dec 1964 (Lewis, formal) vs last freight 27 Feb 1965; 1958 sale to Clinchfield Coal (e-WV) vs a W. M. Ritter lease (american-rails).

properties.line: Buffalo Creek and Gauley: Dundon – Widen
properties.speed_source: estimated from the June 1920 Official Guide card: 18 mi in about 1 hr 25 min, or about 20 km/h. Other years' running times were not computed.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-26), routed with opstrace.py. old_railway_operator probed in Clay County: BC&G (2 ways, the whole line). No 'Buffalo Creek' or 'Buffalo Creek & Gauley' spelling was found. B&O is the Elk River line, not used. OpenHistoricalMap ways named 'Buffalo Creek & Gauley Railroad' (-200367355/-357/-361 etc., ids negated) were fetched with fetch_gap as a cross-check and connector.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 18.1 mi (18.05 mi after simplification) against 18 mi documented (Official Guide 1920, 1939, 1951, 1959; american-rails gives 18.6, Lewis 1975 gives 19). Operator composition from opstrace: 18.0 mi on OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=BC&G (way 15521903 'Buffalo Creek Rail Trail', railway=disused, 18.3 mi Elk River junction - Widen, and way 1456500713 at Widen), 0.2 mi on untagged OpenHistoricalMap rail at the Dundon end. No straight-line legs. Waypoints are OSM place nodes (Dundon, Avoca, Cressmont, Swandale, Eakle, Widen); each is within 0.3 km of the drawn line. The trace starts at the Dundon place node, so the last ~0.2 mi of the tagged way west to the junction at the Elk River is not drawn. The Avoca - Cressmont leg follows Buffalo Creek's meanders at 1.8x its chord, so opstrace's max_ratio was raised from 1.6 to 2.0 for this run. That leg is entirely on the BC&G's own tagged way, so the guard against escaping onto another railroad does not apply. The grade is the modern disused track / Buffalo Creek Trail. No realignment is known, so the drawn alignment is taken to be the 1920-1957 one. That has not been checked against a period map.

segments.note: Buffalo Creek & Gauley passenger service, Dundon (connection with the Coal & Coke Railway, later B&O, across the Elk River from Clay) - Widen, 18 miles. The Official Guide prints the schedule three times: 16 June 1920, two round trips daily except Sunday (leave Widen 6:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m., leave Dundon 8:30 a.m. and 4:45 p.m., about 1 hr 25 min); 1 July 1939, three round trips daily except Sunday; 1 Sept 1951 (Feb 1952 Guide), two round trips daily except Sunday (leave Widen 12:30 and 6:45 p.m., leave Dundon 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m.). Steam trains with combines ran first; from 1941 the runs used Motor A, a 1921 Mack rail bus (american-rails). START 1920 IS [OPEN]: 1920 is the earliest CONFIRMED year (the June 1920 Guide card), not a known opening. The road was chartered in 1904 and reached Widen about 1911, and service before 1920 is likely but no source proves it. Do not move the start earlier without evidence. END 1957 is the last year a contemporary source confirms: Beebe & Clegg, The Age of Steam (1957), says the road 'maintained passenger service through the medium of Mack rail bus'. The real end lies between 1957 and November 1959, when the Guide card reads 'Dundon to Widen (18 miles). Freight service only.' american-rails.com says the two daily round trips ran 'into early 1959' but cites no source, so 1958-1959 are withheld. Extend only if a 1958 Guide card or a last-run story corroborates it. Freight continued to Feb 1965 (formal abandonment 23 Dec 1964 per Lewis 1975), then coal-only revivals 1971-1985 and in the 1990s-1999. None of that is drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE built from the 2-3 daily round trips in the Guide snapshots over a roughly 12-hour day; no Sunday service.
